ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r8.claim: Ittaqā can mean to receive or meet something, as in the cited poem where a woman raises a hand to shield herself from view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r8.anchor: أفمن يتقي: أي يستقبل، كما قال الشاعر: سقط النصيف ولم ترد إسقاطه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r9.claim: Mujahid says the condemned person is dragged on his face through the Fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد: يجر على وجهه في النار، ويجوز أن يعبر بالوجه عن الجملة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the eloquent sense of progressively worsening punishment: the victim first guards himself with limbs, then ultimately with his honored face.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا المعنى عندي أبين بلاغة. في هذا المضمار يجري قول الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r1.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r1.claim: The poem depicts a warrior meeting swords with his face and neck, illustrating boldness in facing a blow without a shield.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r1.anchor: يلقى السيوف بوجهه وبنحره ... ويقيم هامته مقام المغفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies the omitted comparison as one safe from punishment; Ibn Atiyya instead compares him to the blessed in Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r2.anchor: وسوء العذاب: أشده، وخبر من محذوف قدره الزمخشري: كمن أمن العذاب، وابن عطية:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r3.claim: The keepers of Hell address the wrongdoers: taste the consequences of the evil deeds you used to commit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196#2/r3.anchor: وقيل للظالمين: أي قال ذلك خزنة النار، ذوقوا ما كنتم: أي وبال ما كنتم تكسبون

RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r1.claim: Razi says the hard-hearted are doomed to complete worldly misguidance and severe afterlife punishment; he cites 13:33 for the worldly judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r1.anchor: فاعلم أنه تعالى حكم على القاسية قلوبهم بحكم في الدنيا وبحكم في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r2.claim: The face is the body's most honored member: it bears beauty, houses the senses, distinguishes people, and displays happiness or misery; “face” can also name a people's leader or a thing's true aspect.
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r2.anchor: أن أشرف الأعضاء هو الوجه لأنه محل الحسن والصباحة

RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r3.claim: Since people sacrifice every other limb to shield the face, shielding oneself only with the face signifies total inability to ward off punishment; al-Nābigha's mock exception of sword-notches means his people have no real flaw.
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r3.anchor: لا جرم حسن جعل الاتقاء بالوجه كناية عن العجز عن الاتقاء

RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r4.claim: Alternatively, a person cast into Hell has his hands bound to his neck and can ward off the fire only with his face.
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r4.anchor: الذي يلقى في النار يلقى مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه ولا يتهيأ له أن يتقي النار إلا بوجهه

RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r5.claim: The omitted answer completes the comparison: one forced to ward off punishment with his face is not like someone safe from it; he cannot ward it off at all.
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r5.anchor: جوابه محذوف وتقديره أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة كمن هو آمن من العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r6.claim: “Sūʾ al-ʿadhāb” means the severity of punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v26p239/r6.anchor: وسوء العذاب شدته . ثم قال تعالى

STUDYQURAN:39:24/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r1.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r1.claim: An omitted comparison asks whether this person is like one who does right; parallel contrasts appear in 41:40 and 67:22.
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r1.anchor: in security on the Day of Resurrection? (IK, Ṭ) and 67:22

STUDYQURAN:39:24/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r2.claim: Guarding with his face may mean that the face is the first part to touch the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r2.anchor: the first thing to touch the Fire is his face or that he is dragged upon his face into the Fire (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:39:24/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r3.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase may describe someone dragged into the Fire on his face.
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r3.anchor: he is dragged upon his face into the Fire (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:39:24/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:24/r4.claim: Taste that which you used to earn echoes the punishment statement in 7:39.

BURSEVI:v8p75#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p75#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p75#2/r1.claim: The hamza is interrogative denial, the fa connects to an omitted proposition, and the conditional has an omitted predicate: are people equal, when the unbeliever must shield himself with his face, his noblest limb?
BURSEVI:v8p75#2/r1.anchor: الهمزة : للإنكار والفاء : للعطف على محذوف

BURSEVI:v8p75#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p75#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p75#2/r2.claim: اتقى بكذا means making something a shield against what harms oneself; here the unbeliever uses his face as a shield.
BURSEVI:v8p75#2/r2.anchor: يقال : اتقى فلان بكذا إذا جعله وقاية لنفسه والتركيب يدل على دفع شيء عن شيء يضره

BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r1.claim: Al-Kashifi's Persian commentary glosses the evil punishment as the flame of fire.
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r1.anchor: يعني (زبانه آتش) ، كما في "تفسير الفارسي" للكاشفي

BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r2.claim: On Judgment Day the unbeliever's hands are shackled to his neck, unlike the safe believer, so he must ward off punishment with his face.
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r2.anchor: لكون يده التي بها كان يتقي المكاره والمخاوف مغلولة إلى عنقه كمن هو آمن

BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r3.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya reads it as turning one's face toward the evil punishment to fend it off, unlike one who does not protect himself and wrongs himself.
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r3.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {أفمن يتقى بوجهه} توجه {وجهه} {سواء العذاب}

BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r4.claim: The wrongdoers are those who substituted disbelief for faith, denial for affirmation, and disobedience for obedience; the command is spoken by the keepers of Hell.
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r4.anchor: الذين وضعوا الكفر موضع الإيمان والتكذيب موضع التصديق والعصيان موضع الطاعة

BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r5.claim: The past-tense wording signals certainty; naming them explicitly as wrongdoers records their guilt and explains the order to taste punishment.
BURSEVI:v8p75#3/r5.anchor: وصيغة الماضي للدلالة على التحقيق ووضع المظهر في مقام المضمر للتسجيل عليهم بالظلم

BURSEVI:v8p76/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p76/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p76/r1.claim: Their recompense is what they continually earned in worldly life through disbelief, denial, and sins.
BURSEVI:v8p76/r1.anchor: وبال ما كنتم تكسبونه في الدنيا على الدوام من الكفر والتكذيب والمعاصي

BURSEVI:v8p76/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p76/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p76/r2.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says they had been within punishment through vile acts and traits but did not taste it while asleep in heedlessness; death awakened them to it.

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r3.claim: The verse contrasts the people of punishment with those secure from it, representing the misguided and the guided and continuing the previous verse.
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r3.anchor: مقايسة بين أهل العذاب يوم القيامة والآمنين منه

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r4.claim: The interrogative is rejecting; the predicate after “whoever” is omitted, understood as “like one who is safe from it.”
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r4.anchor: محذوف والتقدير كمن هو في أمن منه

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī construes “on the Day of Resurrection” as modifying “guards himself.”

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r6.claim: One view says the person shields himself with his face because his hand, normally used to ward off harm, is shackled to his neck.
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r6.anchor: كذا قيل. وقيل الاتقاء بوجهه بالمعنى المذكور

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī objects that the face is not a means of shielding oneself; an alternative reading makes the phrase refer to warding off future punishment through piety, but he finds it forced.
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r7.anchor: وقيل الاتقاء بوجهه بالمعنى المذكور لا وجه له

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r8.claim: The speakers telling the wrongdoers to taste the result of their deeds are the angels of the Fire; the clause may include an implied qad or not.
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن الجملة بتقدير قد أو بدونه

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r9.claim: Calling them “the wrongdoers” instead of using a pronoun identifies their wrongdoing as the cause of the sentence.
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r9.anchor: لكن وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير للدلالة على علة الحكم

TABRISI:39:23-25/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:23-25/r9.claim: The question contrasts one who wards off punishment with his face on Judgment Day and one who comes safe from the Fire; the face is named because it is a person's most honored part.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r9.anchor: تقديره أفحال من يدفع عذاب الله بوجهه يوم القيامة كحال من يأتي منا لا تمسه النار

TABRISI:39:23-25/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r10.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:39:23-25/r10.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says this is the person thrown into Hell face-first, so the face is the first part touched by the Fire.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه أمن يلقى في النار منكوسا فأول عضو منه مسته النار وجهه عن عطاء

TABRISI:39:23-25/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r11.speaker: عنترة
TABRISI:39:23-25/r11.claim: The verb means to shield oneself; ʿAntara's line describes people advancing him to battle to protect themselves from the spears' heat.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r11.anchor: عنترة: إذ يتقون بي الأسنة لم أخم عنها ولكني تضايق مقدمي

TABRISI:39:23-25/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:23-25/r12.claim: The keepers of Hell tell the wrongdoers to taste the recompense for the sins they committed.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r12.anchor: أي جزاء ما كسبتموه من المعاصي

TABRISI:39:23-25/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:23-25/r16.claim: The verse follows by implying that one who has not followed God's guidance cannot find guidance elsewhere; the face-shielding person remains in disbelief.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r16.anchor: اتصل قوله { أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب } بما قبله

THALABI:v8p232/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p232/r5.claim: سوء العذاب means the severity of punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

THALABI:v8p232/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v8p232/r6.claim: Mujahid says the condemned person is dragged on his face through the Fire.
THALABI:v8p232/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد: يجر على وجهه في النار.

THALABI:v8p232/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r7.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v8p232/r7.claim: Ata says the person is thrown into the Fire upside down, so his face is touched first.
THALABI:v8p232/r7.anchor: وقال عطاء: يرمى به في النار منكوسا، فأول شيء تمسه النار وجهه.

THALABI:v8p232/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r8.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v8p232/r8.claim: Muqatil pictures the unbeliever shackled with a huge sulfur rock at his neck; its heat strikes his face, which he cannot shield with bound hands.
THALABI:v8p232/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هو أن الكافر يرمى به في النار مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه، وفي عنقه صخرة ضخمة مثل الجبل العظيم من الكبريت،

THALABI:v8p232/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p232/r9.claim: The verse elliptically contrasts shielding one's face from punishment with being safe, as in 41:40.
THALABI:v8p232/r9.anchor: ومجاز الآية أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة كمن هو آمن من العذاب وهو كقوله أفمن يلقى في النار خير الآية

THALABI:v8p232/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r10.speaker: المسيب
THALABI:v8p232/r10.claim: Al-Musayyib says this verse was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
THALABI:v8p232/r10.anchor: قال المسيب: نزلت هذه الآية في أبي جهل.

THALABI:v8p232/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p232/r11.claim: An alternative says Hell's keepers tell wrongdoers to taste the consequences of what they earned.
THALABI:v8p232/r11.anchor: وقيل أي: ويقول الخزنة للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون أي: وباله كذب الذين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:24/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:24/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:24/r1.claim: The disbeliever is thrown into the Fire bound and can ward it off only with his face; the rhetorical comparison is with someone who enters Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:24/r1.anchor: وهو الكافر يلقي في النار مغلولا، فلا يتهيأ له أن يتقي النار إلا بوجهه

QASHANI:39:22-24/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r9.claim: The punished person has the face, the noblest organ, exposed because bodily dispositions bind the other limbs and prevent movement to protect himself, unlike one secure from punishment.
QASHANI:39:22-24/r9.anchor: مع كونه أشرف الأعضاء لكون سائر جوارحه مقيدة بهيئات لا يتأتي له التحرز بها ولا يتهيأ، مغللة بأغلال لا يتيسر له بها الحركة في الدفع

ELMALILI:39:22-31/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r3.claim: He pictures the wrongdoer as using his face to shield himself from the evil punishment on Judgment Day.
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r3.anchor: o kötü azâbı yüzü ile koruyacak kimse ne olur?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r1.claim: Commentators see a comparison between two kinds of people: the condemned disbeliever is mentioned, while the implied counterpart is the believer who needs no afterlife protection from fire, deserves happiness, or is in Paradise; these descriptions convey substantially the same idea (Tabari; Shawkani).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r1.anchor: Bunlardan inkârcı olması sebebiyle cehenneme atılacak olan zikredilmekle birlikte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur explains that using one’s face to shield oneself from severe punishment expresses the condemned person’s utter helplessness: even the most valuable part of the body cannot be protected.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r2.anchor: İnsan, bir tehlikeye karşı yüzünü başka bir uzvu ile korumaya çalışır ama yüzünü bir koruma aracı olarak kullanması mümkün değildir. Buna göre

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r3.claim: The wrongdoers are those who commit the greatest injustice by assigning divinity to another or denying God, along with other wrongs; their own deeds and acquisitions bring this fate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:24/r3.anchor: Sonuçta âyet, “zalimler”in yani Allah’a ait olan tanrılığı Allah’tan başkasına tanımak yahut O’nu inkâr etmekle en büyük haksızlığı işleyenlerin ve daha başka haksızlıklar yapanların acıklı durumunu dile getirmekte

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r17.claim: The comparison asks whether one who shields himself with his face from punishment is like one who does not; the unbeliever is thrown into the Fire face-first, while the believer is spared and meets radiance, joy, and honor.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r17.anchor: وقيل إن الكافر يلقى النار أول ما يلقاها بوجهه ؛ لأنه يرمى فيها منكوسا

BURHAN:v2p344/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p344/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p344/r7.claim: A literal comparison question requires an omitted counterpart: here the comparison is with someone enjoying Paradise.
BURHAN:v2p344/r7.anchor: اما اذا كان على حقيقته فلا بد من تقدير المعادل كقوله تعالى ﴿ أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة ﴾ 3 أي كمن ينعم في الجنة

ITQAN:v2p580#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r1.claim: Conjunction may attach to wording, syntactic position, or imagined construction; positional conjunction requires a licit, original position and a live trigger.
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r1.anchor: هو ثلاثة أقسام عطف على اللفظ وهو الأصل وشرطه إمكان توجه العامل إلى المعطوف وعطف على المحل وله ثلاث شروط

ITQAN:v2p580#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r2.claim: Positional-conjunction conditions exclude forms such as “I passed by Zayd and Amr,” a governed adjective plus genitive, and coordination after إن removes the original subject trigger.
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r2.anchor: أحدها إمكان ظهور ذلك المحل في الصحيح فلا يجوز مررت بزيد وعمرا لأنه لا يجوز مررت زيدا

ITQAN:v2p580#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r5.claim: Conjunction by imagined construction requires that the imagined particle could actually occur; it is strongest when common, as in a genitive phrase and Zuhayr’s line.
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r5.anchor: وعطف التوهم نحو ليس زيد قائما ولا قاعد بالخفض على توهم دخول الباء في الخبر وشرط جوازه صحة دخول ذلك العامل المتوهم

ITQAN:v2p580#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r6.speaker: زهير
ITQAN:v2p580#2/r6.claim: Zuhayr’s line supplies a poetic example of genitive conjunction by imagining a preposition in the construction.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r1.speaker: المتنبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r1.claim: Al-Mutanabbi replaces the ordinary reason for a patron’s killing enemies—removing danger—with the claim that he avoids disappointing the wolves’ hopes.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r1.anchor: مثاله قول المتنبي ( ما به قتل أعاديه ولكن يتقى إخلاف ما ترجو الذئاب )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r2.claim: This invented cause praises extraordinary generosity: the patron goes to war because wolves expect sustenance from the slain and he cannot bear to disappoint those who hope.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r2.anchor: أن يبالغ في وصفه بالسخاء والجود وأن طبيعة الكرم قد غلبت عليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r3.claim: The author adds that decisive victory prevents enemies from returning and spares further bloodshed; the image also distinguishes the patron from one who kills excessively from rage, while retaining the stated praise of his traits.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r3.anchor: يهزم العدا ويكسرهم كسرا لا يطمعون بعده في المعاودة فيستغنى بذلك عن قتلهم وإراقة دمائهم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r4.claim: Abu Talib al-Maʾmuni pictures a generous minister sleeping in hope of dreaming a late visitor seeking aid; the author warns that overexplaining the image could imply few people seek his gifts and weaken the praise.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p257/r4.anchor: قول أبى طالب المامونى في قصيدة يمدح بها بعض الوزراء ببخارى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r1.claim: A comparison based on rain does not work here as an identity metaphor: the intended likeness cannot be recovered if the compared people are simply called rainclouds.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r1.anchor: ولا تضمر مثلا ألبتة على حد هو أسد لم يجز لأنه لا معنى لجعلهم صيبا في هذا الموضع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r2.claim: No noun class is inherently barred from metaphor: ṣayyib can describe abundant generosity in another context, as in “a raincloud flowed from him.”
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r2.anchor: فاض صيب منه تريد جوده وهو صيب يفيض تريد يتدفق في الجود

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r3.claim: Metaphor transfers a name naturally when its defining likeness is a familiar, conventional trait, such as the sun’s brightness, a lion’s courage, or the sea’s abundance.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r3.anchor: أن الشبه إذا كان وصفا معروفا في الشيء قد جرى العرف بأن يشبه من أجله به

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r4.claim: A feature not conventionally associated with the sun, such as roundness, cannot be conveyed by calling something the sun; use a sphere, where roundness is salient.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r4.anchor: ولو أنك أردت من الشمس الاستدارة لم يجز أن تدل عليه بالاستعارة ولكن إن أردتها من الفلك جاز

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r5.claim: Where metaphor succeeds, hyperbolic identification is even easier for an audience to accept, as in calling people stars or lions.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p216/r5.anchor: متى صلحت الاستعارة في شيء فالمبالغة فيه أصلح وطريقها أوضح

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r1.claim: Jurjani praises Abu Firas’s arrow simile as rationally grounded and credits him with originating its artistic insight.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r1.anchor: تراه عقليا عريقا في نسبه معترفا بقوة سببه وهو على ذلك من فوائد أبي فراس التي هو أبو عذرها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r2.claim: Metaphor is not imaginative falsehood: it asserts a likeness rather than the literal meaning of the borrowed word.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r2.anchor: الاستعارة لا تدخل في قبيل التخييل لأن المستعير لا يقصد إلى إثبات معنى اللفظة المستعارة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r3.claim: The Qur’anic “the head blazed with gray” means gray hair spreading like a blaze, not literal combustion.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r3.anchor: كقوله عز وجل واشتعل الرأس شيبا ثم لا شبهة في أن ليس المعنى على إثبات الاشتعال ظاهرا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r4.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r4.claim: The Prophet’s saying compares a believer to a mirror, in the sense of a polished surface that reveals what would otherwise go unseen.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r4.anchor: قول النبي المؤمن مرآة المؤمن ليس على إثبات المرآة من حيث الجسم الصقيل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r5.claim: The believer is a mirror because he advises his fellow and shows him his good and bad qualities, as a mirror reveals the viewer’s face.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r5.anchor: إن المؤمن ينصح أخاه ويريه الحسن من القبيح كما ترى المرآة الناظر فيها ما يكون بوجهه من الحسن وخلافه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r6.claim: “Beware the green growth on dung” evokes attractive appearance with a corrupt origin, not the literal meanings of the words.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r6.anchor: وكذا قوله إياكم وخضراء الدمن معلوم أن ليس القصد إثبات معنى ظاهر اللفظين ولكن الشبه الحاصل من مجموعهما

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r7.claim: Jurjani rejects the claim that expressive range requires a statement to contradict fact; truthful speech still offers a broad field for invention.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p238/r7.anchor: مع لزوم الصدق والثبوت على محض الحق الميدان الفسيح والمجال الواسع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r1.claim: Al-Jurjānī prefers the modern poet’s repeated word because the second occurrence adds a real benefit, whereas Abū Tammām’s repeated “madhhab” adds little beyond repeated sounds.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r1.anchor: رأيت الفائدة ضعفت في الأول ، وقويت في الثاني

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r2.claim: Wordplay, especially complete paronomasia such as najā/najā, can adorn poetry and speech when it strengthens meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r2.anchor: ولهذه النكتة كان التجنيس وخصوصا المستوفى منه مثل : ' نجا ونجا ' من حلي الشعر والقول

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r3.claim: This comparison confirms that Qurʾānic inimitability cannot rest on mere phonetic ease; al-Jurjānī turns to explain the causes that make one arrangement excel another.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p380/r3.anchor: استحالة أن يكون الإعجاز في مجرد السهولة وسلامة الألفاظ مما يثقل على اللسان

AKHFASH:v2p495/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p495/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p495/r1.claim: The wording has no expressed predicate; its sense is whether one who shields himself from punishment is better than one who does not.
AKHFASH:v2p495/r1.anchor: فهذا لم يظهر له خبر في اللفظة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r1.claim: Ilā is a preposition originally marking an endpoint or limit; min marks a starting point and ilā the endpoint.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r1.anchor: ' إلى ' : حرف من حروف الخفض . وهي موضوعة في الأصل للانتهاء والغاية .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r2.speaker: أبو زكريا يحيى بن علي التبريزي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r2.claim: Al-Tabrīzī says ilā marks an endpoint in place and elsewhere; reaching it may include entering it or stopping before entry.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r2.anchor: قال أبو زكريا يحيى بن علي التبريزي : وهي للغاية في المكان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r3.claim: For ablution, the endpoint is included: the elbows are included in washing the hands up to them.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r3.anchor: فمما جاء في التنزيل دخل الحد في المحدود قوله تعالى : ^ ( وأيديكم إلى المرافق ) ^ . فالمرافق داخلة في الغسل الواجب .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r4.claim: For fasting, the endpoint is excluded: night itself is not part of the required fast ending at night.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r4.anchor: ومما جاء ولم يدخل الحد في المحدود قوله : ^ ( ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل ) ^ ، فالليل غير داخل في وجوب الصوم .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r5.claim: In its original sense, ilā marks direction or an endpoint; examples include going to Pharaoh and to peoples.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r5.anchor: أحدها : ورودها على أصلها . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r6.claim: A second sense is maʿa, with or together with, as in God’s helpers, combining property, and ablution limits.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r6.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى ' مع ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصف : ﴿ من أنصاري إلى الله ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r7.claim: A third reported sense is lām, as in gathering people for the Day of Resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r7.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى اللام . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام : ﴿ ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r8.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r8.claim: Some instead say ilā in the gathering example means fī, within or on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r8.anchor: وقيل إنه بمعنى ' في ' . و ألحق بعضهم وجها رابعا فقال

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r9.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r9.claim: Some add a fourth sense, biʾ, in phrases about withdrawing to devils and relations with wives; others include these under maʿa, as did al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r9.anchor: و ' إلى ' بمعنى : الباء . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r10.speaker: النضر بن شميل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r10.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl treats the cited ilā examples as meaning maʿa, with.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p102/r10.anchor: وممن قال ذلك النضر بن شميل

FARRA:v2p418/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p418/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p418/r3.claim: It is said that guards drag the disbeliever shackled to the Fire and cast him in, leaving his face as the only protection; the question's answer is implicit.
FARRA:v2p418/r3.anchor: يقال: إن الكافر تنطلق به الخزنة إلى النار مغلولا، فيقذف به في النار

NAHHAS:v4p8/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r12.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v4p8/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies the omitted comparison: is the one who guards himself better, or the one who is blessed?
NAHHAS:v4p8/r12.anchor: حذف الجواب قال الأخفش سعيد أي أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب أفضل أم من سعد

SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies the comparison with one safe from punishment.

SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya supplies the comparison with those blessed in Paradise.
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r4.anchor: أو كالمنعمين في الجنة، وهو تقدير ابن عطية

ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r7.claim: The comparison omits its answer: the person shielding himself from punishment is unlike the one who enters Paradise.
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r7.anchor: هذا مما جوابه محذوف، المعنى كمن يدخل الجنة

ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r8.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r8.claim: Tafsir says the unbeliever is cast into Hell bound and can shield himself from the fire only with his face.
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r8.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الكافر يلقى في النار مغلولا، لا يتهيأ له أن يتقي النار إلا بوجهه

ASAD-NOTES:39:24#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:24#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:24#n31/r1.claim: Protecting oneself with one's face is an idiom meaning that the person has nothing whatever with which to shield himself.
ASAD-NOTES:39:24#n31/r1.anchor: an idiomatic phrase implying that the person concerned has nothing whatever with which to protect himself.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p602/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p602/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p602/r1.claim: Some Arabic scholars were wary of interpreting Qur'anic ambiguities, rare words, and alleged antonyms.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p602/r1.anchor: من علماء العربية من تحرجوا كذلك من تأويل المتشابه والغريب والأضداد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p602/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p602/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم السجستاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p602/r3.claim: The Basran linguist and Qur'an scholar Abu Hatim was strongly cautious about interpreting Qur'anic antonyms and criticized those who ventured beyond their Arabic knowledge.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p602/r3.anchor: وأبو حاتم السجستاني، من أعلام البصريين علماء اللغة والقرآن

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r6.claim: The enunciative khabar is suppressed in the interrogative sentence, and Islahi supplies it in his translation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r6.anchor: The enunciative ( khabar) in this interrogative sentence also is suppressed. I have tried to unfold it in the translation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r7.claim: The punishment will be so terrible that the arrogant will try to use their faces as shields, with no other protection available.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r7.anchor: compelled to put forth their faces as their shields – faces with which they used to show arrogance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r8.claim: The face is a person’s most valued and protected part, making its use as a shield an especially stark reversal.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r8.anchor: The noblest and dearest part of a person’s body is his face.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r9.claim: The wrongdoers are the arrogant people who rejected the Qur’an and thereby wronged themselves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r9.anchor: refers to the arrogant people under discussion. This is because by rejecting the Qur’ān they were guilty of wronging their souls.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r10.claim: God will show no mercy at the helplessness of wrongdoers when they face punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r10.anchor: The verse states that the Almighty will not have any mercy

QIRAAT-ER:39:24:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:24:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:39:24:11#1/r1.claim: Vowel harmony gives qīla a rounded transitional vowel after wāw while retaining the passive q-w-l form.
QIRAAT-ER:39:24:11#1/r1.anchor: Canonical vowel-harmony reading gives qīla a rounded transitional vowel after wa

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r1.claim: The verse resumes the argument to explain the contrast between the guided and the astray.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r1.anchor: استئناف جار مجرى التعليل لما قبله من تباين حال المهتدي والضال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r2.claim: The omitted premise is “are all people equal?”: is the person forced to ward off punishment with his face like one safe from harm and in no need of protection?
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r2.anchor: التقدير أكل الناس سواء فمن شأنه أن يتقي بوجهه الذي هو أشرف أعضائه يوم القيامة العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r3.claim: The face is literal: his hand, which once warded off harms, is chained to his neck, leaving him to shield himself with his most honored limb.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r3.anchor: فالوجه على حقيقته وقد يحمل على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r4.claim: Even without the report that the hand is chained, taking the face literally vividly depicts the completeness and earnestness of his self-protection.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r4.anchor: وقد يحمل على ذلك من غير حاجة إلى حديث كون اليد مغلولة تصويرا لكمال اتقائه وجده فيه وهو أبلغ

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r5.claim: The face may mean the whole person, making the image hyperbolic.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الوجه بمعنى الجملة والمبالغة عليه دون المبالغة فيما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r6.claim: Another view treats face-protection as a figure for having no shield at all, since the face is not a means of protection; Alusi finds this strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r6.anchor: وقيل الإتقاء بالوجه كناية عن عدم ما يتقى به إذ الإتقاء بالوجه لا وجه له لأنه لا يتقي به ولا يخلو عن خدش

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r7.claim: “On the Day of Resurrection” may be governed by “protects himself,” or attached to “the evil of punishment,” meaning the punishment of that Day; Alusi calls the latter sound but the former more immediate.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r7.anchor: معمول يتقي كما أشرنا إلى ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r8.claim: The cited line depicts the literal face and chest meeting swords, with the head serving as a helmet.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r8.anchor: يلقى السيوف بوجهه وبنحره ويقيم هامته مقام المغفر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r9.claim: Alusi says the verse was revealed about Abu Jahl.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r10.claim: “It was said to the wrongdoers” may coordinate with “protects himself”; the past tense signals certainty. Alternatively, it is a circumstantial clause, with or without an implied “already.”
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r10.anchor: عطف على يتقي أي ويقال لهم من جهة خزنة النار وصيغة الماضي للدلالة على التحقق والتقرر وقيل الواو للحال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r11.claim: The explicit noun “wrongdoers” replaces a pronoun to condemn them and signal why they are told to taste punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r11.anchor: ووضع المظهر موضع المضمر للتسجيل عليهم بالظلم والإشعار بعلة الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r12.claim: They are commanded to taste the continuing consequence of their worldly earnings in disbelief and sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260#2/r12.anchor: أي وبال ما كنتم تكسبون في الدنيا على الدوام من الكفر والمعاصي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r1.claim: The “evil” of punishment means its severity.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r2.claim: Mujahid says the condemned person is dragged face first through Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: يجر على وجهه في النار. وقال عطاء:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r3.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r3.claim: Ata says the person is thrown into Hell upside down, so the face is the first part touched by the fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء: يرمى به في النار منكوسا فأول شيء منه تمسه النار وجهه. قال مقاتل:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r4.claim: Muqatil describes the unbeliever bound with his hands to his neck and a huge sulfur rock at his neck; its fire and heat strike his face, which the bonds prevent him from shielding.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل: هو أن الكافر يرمى به في النار مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه، وفي عنقه صخرة مثل جبل عظيم من الكبريت،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r5.claim: The verse's implied comparison asks whether one guarding his face from punishment can be like someone safe from punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117/r5.anchor: ومجاز الآية: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب كمن هو آمن من العذاب؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117#2/r1.claim: The ones saying “taste what you earned” are the keepers of Hell; what the wrongdoers taste is the consequence of their deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p117#2/r1.anchor: {وقيل} يعني: تقول الخزنة، {للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون} أي: وباله.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.claim: An accusative noun for an ongoing visible action can replace an omitted verb phrase; the situation supplies the verb, and the noun functions like a verbal noun.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.anchor: فكأنه لفظ بقوله أتقوم قائما وأتقعد قاعدا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.speaker: منهم
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.claim: Sībawayh records a variant construction عائذ بالله من شر فلان alongside the accusative عائذا بالله.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.anchor: ومنهم من يقول عائذ بالله من شر فلان

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.claim: Ibn al-Harith al-Sahmi's poetic وعائذا بك is understood as وعياذا بك, supporting the noun's substitution for an omitted verb; Sībawayh also gives زحارا أنانا for زحيرا وأنينا.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأقائماوقدقعدالناسوأقاعد.claim: A second poetic example uses the accusatives زحارا أنانا in place of the verbal nouns زحيرا وأنينا, with the omitted verbs understood from the construction.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: Frequent سدس becomes ست: speakers substitute t for the first s before assimilating d to t, avoiding an even heavier cluster of sibilants; ṣād is not chosen as the substitute.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: أبدلوا مكان السين أشبه الحروف بها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: The imperfect variants ييجل and أدل alter the initial sequence to ease wāw next to yāʾ; kasra helps convert wāw to yāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: قولهم ييجل كسروا ليقلبوا الواو ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: The form ود comes from وتد in Tamim speech by silencing t and assimilating it to d; this is irregular because it risks ambiguity, so speakers also use clearer forms such as وتد.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: وتد وهي الحجازية الجيدة ولكن بني تميم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: Sībawayh records عتدان and عدان as ways of avoiding the difficult tāʾ-dāl sequence, with عدان patterned after ود.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: قولهم عتدان وقال بعضهم عتدان فرارا من هذا وقد قالوا عدان شبهوه بود

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: Frequent forms such as أحست، مست، and ظلت drop one of a doubled consonant because speakers dislike gemination and moving a consonant that normally cannot take a vowel.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: أحست ومست وظلت لما كثر في كلامهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: The common form يسطيع deletes t from يستطيع because the t-ṭ sequence is heavy and assimilating t to emphatic ṭ would require moving the normally fixed sīn.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: كما حذفوا التاء من قولهم يستطيع فقالوا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: An alternative analysis derives يسطيع by adding sīn to أطاع يطيع as compensation for the silence at the verb's ʿayn position.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: من زاد السين على أطاع يطيع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: Frequent forms with two adjacent tāʾs, including يَتَّقِى and يتسع, delete one tāʾ; Sībawayh likens this to deletion in doubled roots.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: ومن الشاذ قولهم تقيت وهو يتقي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: بعض العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: Some Arabs use استخذ for اتخذ, substituting sīn for tāʾ to avoid the doubled tāʾ sequence.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: A second account derives استخذ from استفعل after deleting a tāʾ from استتخذ to avoid gemination, as in ظلت.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: بعض العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: Some Arabs say الطجع for اضطجع, replacing emphatic ḍād with lām to avoid two emphatic consonants together.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: قول بعض العرب الطجع في اضطجع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: One analysis of يستيع from يستطيع deletes ṭāʾ, as in ظلت, retaining the other augmentation as in تقيت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: حذف الطاء كما حذف لام ظلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: The alternative analysis replaces ṭāʾ with t so the consonant after sīn is voiceless, paralleling voiced substitution in ازدان.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: In tribal names whose definite article is pronounced, the nūn is deleted before its nearby lām through frequent cross-boundary easing; where the article is not pronounced, this deletion does not occur.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.claim: Some speakers shorten على الماء to علماء بنو فلان by deleting lām, which Sībawayh accepts as Arabic.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانشاذامماخففواعلىألسن.anchor: على الماء بنو فلان وهي عربية

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r1.claim: The punished person uses his face as a shield because his hands are chained to his neck, leaving no other way to ward off torment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r1.anchor: يجعله درقة يقي به نفسه لأنه يكون يداه مغلولة إلى عنقه فلا يقدر أن يتقي إلا بوجهه

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r2.claim: The comparison is with someone safe from punishment; the predicate is omitted, as in similar constructions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r2.anchor: كمن هو آمن منه، فحذف الخبر كما حذف في نظائره

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r3.claim: The overt description wrongdoers replaces a pronoun to register their wrongdoing and identify why they are addressed this way.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r3.anchor: فوضع الظاهر موضعه تسجيلا عليهم بالظلم وإشعارا بالموجب

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r4.claim: They are told to taste the consequence of what they earned; the waw is circumstantial with an implicit qad.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:24-26/r4.anchor: أي وباله، والواو للحال وقد مقدرة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r1.claim: After contrasting the expanded and constricted breast and concluding that one is guided and the other astray, the passage unfolds each group’s outcome in a deliberately interwoven interrogative; misguidance leads to punishment and guidance to bliss.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r1.anchor: شرع في بيان ما لكل منهما نشرا مشوشا في أسلوب الإنكار أيضا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r2.claim: The singular follows the form من so the wording does not suggest that the faces are those of leaders; the face becomes a shield because the hand, normally used to ward off danger, is bound, and the honored face must protect the rest of the body.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r2.anchor: وأفرد على لفظ { من } لئلا يظن أن الوجوه الأكابر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r3.claim: The wrongdoer is thrown upside down into Hell, bound, with no free limb to shield his face; a mountain-like sulfur stone hangs at his neck and he is dragged face-first, unlike the one who receives bliss in heart and body.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r3.anchor: لأنه يرمي به في النار منكوسا وهو مكبل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r4.claim: The passive وقيل fits the general character of reproach; the text could have said “to him,” but instead names the wrongdoers and uses the plural to generalize the judgment and show their numbers do not help them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r4.anchor: ولما كان مطلق التوبيخ والتقريع متكئا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r5.claim: The wrongdoers are those who abandoned guidance, followed desire, and went astray while leading others astray.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r5.anchor: أي الذين تركوا طريق الهدى واتبعوا الهوى فضلوا وأضلوا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r6.claim: They are told to taste the recompense of what they used to regard as the benefit and fruit of their deeds and conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r6.anchor: أي جزاء ما { كنتم تكسبون * } أي تعدونه فائدة وثمرة لأعمالكم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r7.claim: By ellipsis through correspondence, the opening question implies the omitted counterpart, and the words addressed to wrongdoers imply that the righteous are told to be content and take delight as recompense for their deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p440/r7.anchor: ذكر الاستفهام أولا دليلا على حذف متعلقه ثانيا

DURR-FULL:v7p222/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r6.claim: Mujahid says the condemned person is dragged on his face through the Fire, comparing this to the question in 41:40 about who is safer on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة} قال: يجر على وجهه في النار

DURR-FULL:v7p222/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the condemned person is taken bound to Hell and thrown in, so that his face is the first part touched by the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: ينطلق به إلى النار مكتوفا ثم يرمى فيها فأول ما تمس وجهه النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r6.claim: The verse interrupts Qur’an-praise before 39:27; commentators connect it to the two outcomes in 39:23, with an omitted comparison and a reportive or rejecting question: the punished and the blessed are not equal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r6.anchor: وجعلها المفسرون تفريعا على جملة { ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r7.claim: The omitted comparison is with one safe from punishment through God’s guidance, as in the parallel question at 47:14; the guided do not suffer the torment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r7.anchor: والقول فيه مثل القول في سابقه من الاستفهام وحذف الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAshur’s preferred construction makes the question identify the referent of “whoever God leads astray” in 39:23: the omitted subject is “is he the one who shields his face from torment?”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r1.anchor: تفريعا لتعيين ما صدق ( من ) في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r2.claim: Ittiqāʾ means undertaking protection, restraint, and warding off; waqā takes two objects and may mark the instrument of protection with bi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r2.anchor: وفعلها يتعدى إلى مفعولين ، يقال : وقى نفسه ضرب السيف ، ويتعدى بالباء إلى سبب الوقاية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r3.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r3.claim: Al-Nābigha’s verse, “she protected us with her hand,” illustrates bi marking the means by which protection is achieved.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r3.anchor: وقال النابغة : سقط النصيف ولم ترد إسقاطه فتناولته واتقتنا باليد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r4.claim: With the iftiʿāl form, the verb takes one object, which was the second object of the base verb waqā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r4.anchor: وأصله مفعول ثان إذ أصله : وقى نفسه سوء العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r5.claim: Since the face is most precious and normally shielded from blows, claiming to shield oneself with one’s face is sarcastic allusion to having no protection; compare 18:29.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r5.anchor: مستعملا كناية عن عدم الوقاية على طريقة التهكم أو التلميح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r6.claim: “The evil of the torment” is the object of ittqā; in the base construction it is the second object of waqā, but the derived form governs one object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r6.anchor: و { سوء العذاب } منصوب على المفعولية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r7.claim: “And it was said” may be coordinated with the relative clause, with “whoever” understood collectively as “they”; “the wrongdoers” replaces a pronoun to imply their punishment is caused by their shirk.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r7.anchor: يجوز أن يكون { وقيل } عطفا على الصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r8.claim: The one with no shield against punishment is told to taste the torment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r8.anchor: تنجيه من ذوق العذاب فيقال لهم : ذوقوا العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r9.claim: Alternatively, “the wrongdoers” broadly includes polytheists from all peoples; the sentence then sums up their common fate and leads into the denial by earlier peoples in 39:25.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p393/r9.anchor: جميع الذين أشركوا بالله من الأمم غير خاص بالمشركين المتحدث عنهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r1.claim: The past form depicts a certain future as already past; alternatively, the clause is circumstantial with an implicit قد, so the tense needs no such reinterpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r1.anchor: وجاء فعل { وقيل } بصيغة المضي وهو واقع في المستقبل لأنه لتحقق وقوعه نزل منزلة فعل مضى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r2.claim: Taste is a metaphor for bodily sensation: the tongue's sense is stronger than the skin's, and the comparison rests on intensity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r2.anchor: والذوق : مستعار لإحساس ظاهر الجسد لأن إحساس الذوق باللسان أشد من إحساس ظاهر الجلد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r3.claim: The tasted punishment repays their worldly acquisition of shirk and its practices; equating punishment with their deeds stresses just recompense corresponding to their actions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r3.anchor: والمذوق : هو العذاب فهو جزاء ما اكتسبوه في الدنيا من الشرك وشرائعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r4.claim: The wording تكسبون instead of تعملون attributes the punishment to what they acquired, cutting off the protest of people who resent their torment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p394/r4.anchor: فجيء بالصلة الدالة على أن ما ذاقوه جزاء ما اكتسبوه قطعا لتبرمهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r1.claim: The third kind of revelation occasion is a recurring sort of event involving one person; the verse announces its rule and rebukes whoever commits it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r1.anchor: وبيان أحكامها وزجر من يرتكبها ، فكثيرا ما تجد المفسرين وغيرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r2.claim: Exegetes saying a verse was revealed about an event may mean that the event is one example covered by the verse, not its exclusive occasion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r2.anchor: المفسرين وغيرهم يقولون نزلت في كذا وكذا ، وهم يريدون أن من الأحوال التي تشير إليها تلك الآية تلك الحالة الخاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet’s warning that one who swears falsely to seize a Muslim’s property will meet God angry; revelation confirmed this warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r3.anchor: أن عبد الله بن مسعود قال : قال رسول الله من حلف على يمين صبر يقتطع بها مال امرئ مسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r4.speaker: الأشعث بن قيس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r4.claim: Ashath ibn Qays said the verse about the false oath was revealed concerning him and a well on his cousin’s land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r4.anchor: فدخل الأشعث بن قيس فقال ما حدثكم أبو عبد الرحمن ? فقالوا كذا وكذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r5.claim: Ibn Masud treated the verse as general confirmation of a general prophetic report, whereas Ashath took his own “it was revealed about me” as exclusive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r5.anchor: فابن مسعود جعل الآية عامة لأنه جعلها تصديقا لحديث عام ? والأشعث بن قيس ظنها خاصة به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas said they called the opening passages about hypocrites in Surat al-Tawba “the exposer.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r6.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس : كنا نسمي سورة التوبة سورة الفاضحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r7.claim: The verse about disbelievers not wanting good to descend is another case where no special occasion needs to be supplied merely because some Jews showed Muslims affection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r7.anchor: فلا حاجة لبيان أنها نزلت لما أظهر بعض اليهود مودة المؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r8.claim: Storytellers and some exegetes overemphasize this kind of occasion without benefit; it can mislead less informed readers into restricting a verse whose wording does not visibly state its generality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r8.anchor: وهذا القسم قد أكثر من ذكره أهل القصص وبعض المفسرين ولا فائدة في ذكره ، على أن ذكره قد يوهم القاصرين قصر الآية على تلك الحادثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r9.claim: The fourth kind is an event whose circumstances fit the meaning of surrounding Qur’anic passages, so early Muslims may seem to identify it as the specific occasion when they mean it falls under the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r9.anchor: والرابع : هو حوادث حدثت وفي القرآن آيات تناسب معانيها سابقة أو لاحقة فيقع في عبارات بعض السلف ما يوهم أن تلك الحوادث هي المقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r10.claim: Many disagreements among Companions over occasions of revelation illustrate this fourth kind; al-Suyuti discusses it with examples in the fifth issue of his al-Itqan treatment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r10.anchor: وجود اختلاف كثير بين الصحابة في كثير من أسباب النزول كما هو مبسوط في المسألة الخامسة من بحث أسباب النزول من الإتقان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that a man with a small flock greeted pursuing Muslims with salam, was killed as a supposed unbeliever, and had his flock taken; the verse then came down.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r11.anchor: أن ابن عباس قرأ قوله تعالى ) ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا ( بألف بعد لام السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r12.claim: The story must have happened, since Ibn Abbas transmitted it, but the verse was not revealed exclusively for it; its context places it among rules of jihad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r12.anchor: فالقصة لابد أن تكون قد وقعت لأن ابن عباس رواها لكن الآية ليست نازلة فيها بخصوصها ولكن نزلت في أحكام الجهاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r13.speaker: الزبير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r13.claim: After his water dispute with an Ansari at the streams of al-Harra, al-Zubayr said he thought the verses about submitting disputes to the Prophet had been revealed about that event.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r13.anchor: بعد أن ذكر نزاع الزبير والأنصاري في ماء شراج الحرة قال الزبير : فما أحسب هذه الآيات إلا نزلت في ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r14.speaker: الزركشي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r14.claim: Al-Zarkashi says a Companion or Successor who says “revealed about this” commonly means the verse includes that ruling, not that this event caused its revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r14.anchor: قال السيوطي في الإتقان عن الزركشي قد عرف من عادة الصحابة والتابعين أن أحدهم إذا قال نزلت هذه الآية في كذا ، فإنه يريد بذلك أنها تتضمن هذا الحكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r15.speaker: ابن تيمية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r15.claim: Ibn Taymiyya records disagreement over whether a Companion’s “revealed about this” is a transmitted report or exegesis: al-Bukhari counts it as musnad, while most hadith compilers do not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r15.anchor: وفيه عن ابن تيمية قد تنازع العلماء في قول الصحابي : نزلت هذه الآية في كذا ، هل يجري مجرى المسند أو يجري مجرى التفسير ?

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r16.speaker: ابن تيمية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r16.claim: Ibn Taymiyya distinguishes a general “revealed about this” statement from an account naming an event immediately preceding revelation, which all compilers treat as musnad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p48/r16.anchor: بخلاف ما إذا ذكر سببا نزلت عقبه فإنهم كلهم يدخلونه في المسند

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r1.claim: The question expresses amazement and compares the person guarding his face from punishment with those enjoying Paradise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r1.anchor: هذا تقرير بمعنى التعجيب، والمعنى: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب كالمنعمين في الجنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says the person falls face-first into the Fire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r2.anchor: فقال مجاهد: يخر على وجهه في النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r3.claim: One group explains that a disbeliever is bound, hands tied to feet and neck, and cast face-down into Hell, leaving the face as the only means of protection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة: ذلك لما روي أن الكافر يلقى في النار مكتوفا مربوطة يداه إلى رجليه مع عنقه ويكب على وجهه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r4.claim: Another group sees a description of escalating punishment: he first guards himself with all his limbs, until the torment reaches his noblest limb and senses, the face, with no further escape.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة: المعنى صفة كثرة ما ينالهم من العذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r5.claim: The author prefers the escalating-torment reading as more eloquent, illustrated by the poet's image of meeting swords with face and neck as a sign of boldness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r5.anchor: وهذا المعنى عندي أبين بلاغة، وفي هذا المضمار يجري قول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r6.claim: ذوقوا means experience directly or undergo.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ذوقوا عبارة عن باشروا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r7.claim: An omitted word is understood: taste the recompense for what you used to earn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528#2/r7.anchor: وهنا محذوف تقديره: جزاء ما كنتم تكسبون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r1.claim: The phrase means the severity of the punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r1.anchor: أي شدته قال الزجاج جوابه محذوف تقديره كمن يدخل الجنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the comparison's answer is omitted: “like one who enters Paradise.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج جوابه محذوف تقديره كمن يدخل الجنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r3.claim: Commentary says the disbeliever is cast into Hell shackled and can shield himself from it only with his face.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r3.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الكافر يلقى في النار مغلولا ولا يتهيأ له أن يتقيها إلا بوجه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r4.claim: The wrongdoers addressed by Hell's keepers are the disbelievers, told to taste the recompense for their deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178#2/r4.anchor: بقوله ﴿ وقيل للظالمين ﴾ يعني الكافرين ﴿ ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون ﴾ أي جزاء كسبكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95#2/r1.claim: The condemned is reproached with the punishment earned, unlike the person who comes safely on Judgment Day; Ibn Kathīr compares this with face-walking and fire references.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95#2/r1.anchor: ويقرع فيقال له ولأمثاله من الظالمين: {ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95#2/r2.claim: The verse states only one side of the comparison; the poet's line about seeking good leaves its opposite unstated, meaning good or evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95#2/r2.anchor: واكتفى في هذه الآية بأحد القسمين عن الآخر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r1.claim: The two hadiths describe the Quran's companion as being in a blessed, enviable state; one should wish for the same blessing and congratulate him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r1.anchor: ومضمون هذين الحديثين: أن صاحب القرآن في غبطة وهو حسن الحال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r2.claim: Ghibta means wishing for another's blessing without its removal; condemned envy wishes the blessing removed, whether or not the envier gets it, and was Iblis's first sin against Adam.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r2.anchor: وهذا بخلاف الحسد المذموم وهو تمني زوال نعمة المحسود عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r3.claim: The praiseworthy form of hasad is wishing for the same good state, not its loss to someone else.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r3.anchor: والحسد الشرعي الممدوح هو تمني مثل حال ذلك الذي هو على حالة سارة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r4.claim: The Prophet's statement that there is no hasad except in two cases refers to the Quran reader's private blessing and the charitable spender's benefit to others; Ibn Kathir links it to 35:29.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r4.anchor: قال عليه السلام: "لا حسد إلا في اثنتين "، فذكر النعمة القاصرة وهي تلاوة القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r5.claim: Yazid ibn al-Akhnas reports the Prophet saying that competition should be limited to a person devoted to the Quran and a person who gives away wealth in charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r5.anchor: عن يزيد بن الأخنس، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا تنافس بينكم إلا في اثنتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r6.speaker: أبو كبشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r6.claim: Abu Kabsha reports the Prophet dividing people into four: learned and charitable wealth is best; knowledge without wealth earns equal reward when the person intends good; ignorant wealth is squandered; and the poor ignorant person's corrupt wish carries equal burden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p65#3/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد البختري الطائي، عن أبي كبشة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r5.claim: God does not fail to fulfill promise or threat, contrary to what some Murjiʾa maintain.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r5.anchor: وتدل على أنه تعالى لا يخلف الوعد والوعيد، خلاف ما يقوله بعض المرجئة

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r14.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says the verse about facing punishment was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r14.anchor: وقيل: نزل قوله: (أفمن يتقي بوجهه) الآية في أبي جهل، عن سعيد بن المسيب

JISHUMI:v8p6058/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6058/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6058/r1.claim: The comparison is elliptical: the protected person is contrasted with someone safe from punishment, omitted because context supplies it.
JISHUMI:v8p6058/r1.anchor: قلنا: محذوف، تقديره: كمن هو آمن من العذاب، فحذف لدلالة الكلام عليه

JISHUMI:v8p6058/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6058/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6058/r2.claim: The keepers of Hell tell the wrongdoers to taste the consequence and recompense of what they earned.
JISHUMI:v8p6058/r2.anchor: وقيل للظالمين تقوله الخزنة ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون أي: وباله وجزاءه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p123/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p123/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p123/r1.claim: One image is an unbeliever dragged on his face to the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p123/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن الكافر يسحب على وجهه إلى النار يوم القيامة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p123/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p123/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p123/r2.claim: Alternatively, the Fire first reaches the person's face on entering it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p123/r2.anchor: لأن النار تبدأ بوجهه إذا دخلها

MUJAHID:v2p557#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p557#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p557#3/r1.claim: The person shielding himself from punishment is dragged face-first through the Fire; Mujahid links this to 41:40.
MUJAHID:v2p557#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة ﴾ قال يجر على وجهه في النار وهو كقوله ﴿ أفمن يلقى في النار خير أم من يأتي آمنا يوم القيامة ﴾

MUQATIL:39:24-25/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r1.claim: The misguided person who shields his face from intense punishment is unlike the guided person whose face the Fire does not reach.
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r1.anchor: { أفمن يتقى بوجهه سوء } يعنى شدة { العذاب يوم القيامة } يقول: ليس الضال الذى يتقى النار بوجهه كالمهتدى الذى لا تصل النار إلى وجهه

MUQATIL:39:24-25/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r2.claim: The disbeliever is chained with hands to his neck and a mountain-sized burning sulfur stone hanging there; flames scorch his face and his bonds prevent him from shielding it.
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r2.anchor: يقول الكافر يتقى بوجهه شدة العذاب، وهو فى النار مغلولة يده إلى عنقه، وفى عنقه حجر ضخم مثل الجبل العظيم من كبريت

MUQATIL:39:24-25/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r3.claim: The keepers tell wrongdoers to taste punishment for the disbelief and denial they committed.
MUQATIL:39:24-25/r3.anchor: { وقيل } وقالت الخزنة: { للظالمين ذوقوا } العذاب ب { ما كنتم تكسبون } [آية: 24] من الكفر والتكذيب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r1.claim: The omitted comparison asks whether someone shielding himself with his face is like one safe from punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r1.anchor: كمن أمن من العذاب فحذف الخبر كما حذف فى نظائره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r2.claim: The phrase means the severity of punishment.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r3.claim: People shield their precious face with a hand; one thrown into Hell has hands bound to the neck and can shield himself only with his face.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r3.anchor: والذى يلقى فى النار يلقى مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه فلا يتهيأ له أن يتقى النار إلا بوجهه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r4.claim: The speakers are the keepers of Hell, addressing wrongdoers.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p53/r5.claim: What they are told to taste is the recompense of what they earned.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r1.speaker: عطاء وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r1.claim: Ata and Ibn Zayd say the person is thrown shackled into the Fire, with its first contact on his face.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r1.anchor: قال عطاء وابن زيد: يرمى به مكتوفا في النار فأول شيء تمس منه النار وجهه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r2.claim: Mujahid says the person is dragged face-first through the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يجر على وجهه في النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r3.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r3.claim: Muqatil pictures a disbeliever thrown into the Fire with hands chained to the neck and a mountain-sized sulfur rock hanging there; it burns and scorches the face, which the chains prevent him from shielding.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هو أن الكافر يرمى به في النار مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r4.claim: The clause has an omitted predicate or comparison.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r5.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies the comparison: is one who wards off punishment with his face better, or one who is fortunate, as in the cited verse?
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r5.anchor: قال الأخفش: أي { أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب } أفضل أم من سعد

QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r6.claim: The wrongdoers are disbelievers, and their keepers address them in rebuke and reproach.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r7.claim: They are told to taste the recompense for what they earned through sins.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:24-26/r8.claim: The wording is paralleled by the command to taste what was hoarded in the cited verse.
